transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-22
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Product), Jared Cole (Skyline), Maya Ortiz (Skyline), Naveen Rao (Skyline), Lena Park (Skyline security), Tom Baxter (Skyline SRE)

Summary:
Redwood demo focused on evaluation and quality monitoring (Prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons) via the Console and Redwood Optimize. Customer is evaluating a pilot to replace some in-house signal ranking tests for e-commerce search results. Main concerns: metric drift detection sensitivity, false positives on regression alerts, data residency, and integrating Skyline CI to run nightly evals. Next steps captured as action items.

Topics covered:
- Overview of prompt-set driven evals and how Console stores prompt sets
- Setting thresholds and alerting for regression (precision/recall/ctr/NRR)
- A/B comparison flows and rollout strategy (canary -> 50/50 -> rollout)
- Using Optimize to generate batching/quant recommendations to hit latency & cost targets
- Integrations: webhook alerts, PagerDuty, SSO and VPC considerations

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alicia: okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alicia with Redwood Inference, i'll hand over to Marcus in a min to jump into the Console demo, but quick round robin?
[00:08] Jared: yeah Jared Cole, head of search at Skyline, hi all, thanks for doing this, we wanted a focused walkthrough on regressions and ab tests for our search re-ranker
[00:14] Maya: Maya Ortiz, ML infra, i'll be the one wiring up the prompt sets and running the nightly jobs
[00:20] Marcus: great, Marcus Li here, i'm an SE, i'll demo the Console Eval pages, Optimize suggestions, and a quick API flow with streaming responses
[00:28] Priya: Priya Nair, product — i'll be taking notes on feature asks, especially around alert thresholds and historical baselines
[00:34] Lena: Lena Park, InfoSec — we'll need the SOC 2 doc and an auditable history of eval inputs and outputs
[00:40] Tom: Tom Baxter, SRE, mostly here for reliability and any infra changes for private/de-dedicated options
[00:46] Alicia: awesome, thanks. quick context question — do you already store prompt sets in a format today?
[00:52] Jared: we have a bunch of csvs and a half-baked internal service that hits our in-house model, but it's not easy to do side-by-side ab comparisons and alerting, we mostly do manual checks
[01:02] Maya: and we run nightly benchmarks, but the diffs are noisy — we get a lot of false positives when ranking diffs are tiny, so we want better signal and smarter alerting
[01:12] Marcus: perfect, that is exactly the pain Redwood Optimize + Console evals aim to address — i'll share my screen and walk through a sample prompt-set flow
[01:22] [screen share starts — Console Eval page visible]
[01:28] Marcus: here is the Eval homepage — you can create prompt sets, tag them by intent, attach labels for golden answers or business metrics like revenue-per-click, and then define metric suites. the UI stores historical runs and produces regression alerts when thresholds are crossed
[01:41] Marcus: notice the run history on the right — each run includes a diff heatmap, per-prompt breakdown, and an estimated business-impact column. that impact column is plumbed from your mapped KPI (we mapped "click_through" in the demo)
[01:55] Maya: are the metrics computed client-side or do they run in Redwood infra?
[02:00] Marcus: they run in Redwood's eval pipeline — you can choose to run in-hosted or through Dedicated pools for data isolation, the latter gives you a VPC option; the math is done on our side but logs and artifacts can be exported to your S3 if you prefer
[02:14] Lena: S3 export is fine, but we need KMS control and audit logs — can Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[02:20] Alicia: yes, customer-managed KMS for artifacts is supported in Private and Dedicated, and we can surface audit logs in the Console's audit tab. i'll send the SOC 2 + KMS integration doc after the call
[02:30] [00:02:35] Marcus: jumping to regression alerts — you can set alerts at the metric level and at an experiment level. by default there's a statistical test (wilcoxon / bootstrapped CI) plus a business-impact threshold to reduce false positives
[02:47] Marcus: we also have a "sensibility" control — think of it as a tunable parameter: low sensitivity = fewer alerts, high sensitivity = more. it learns over time with configurable rolling baselines
[02:59] Naveen: how do we avoid spurious alerts when our traffic shifts? we have weekly promo spikes
[03:05] Marcus: good question — you can tag runs with traffic-slice metadata and have separate baselines per slice (mobile vs web, promo vs organic). also you can configure the baselines window and exclude outliers automatically
[03:18] Maya: can we attach the exact prompt + model + seed so audits can reproduce results?
[03:23] Marcus: yes, each eval run stores the prompt text, model identifier, tokenizer checksum, and seed; there's a reproducibility link you can click to re-run a specific prompt set against a pinned model version
[03:33] Tom: what about running evaluations as part of our CI? nightly is fine but want to gate releases if there's a regression
[03:39] Marcus: we have a REST endpoint for kicking off eval runs, and a webhook for results; you can wire it to your CI to fail builds or open tickets on regressions. we also integrate with PagerDuty and Slack
[03:48] [03:50] Priya: show us the A/B comparison flow
[03:52] Marcus: sure — switching to the A/B tab, you can define slices, traffic allocation, and rollout policies. this ties into the serving layer so you can point your app to the Redwood API and specify the experiment id in the request header
[04:06] Marcus: live demo now — i trigger an A/B run comparing our baseline model vs a quantized variant. here's the per-prompt delta distribution and the waterfall chart showing where the new model wins/loses by segment
[04:20] Jared: that waterfall looks great, can we restrict to top-100 search queries?
[04:24] Marcus: yes, you can upload a keyset or filter by frequency — the UI lets you focus the analysis on the most impactful queries
[04:30] Maya: how do you compute "business impact"? is it simulated or actual?
[04:34] Marcus: it's simulated by default using your mapping function (we ask for a conversion weight per query type), but if you can provide historical ground-truth click/revenue data we can compute an empirical impact metric
[04:44] Marcus: switching to Optimize — Optimize looks at your request distribution and suggests batching sizes, quantization profiles, and KV cache settings to hit latency and cost objectives while preserving quality
[04:54] Marcus: here's an Optimize recommendation — it suggested int8 quant for a large fraction of requests, a smaller batch for low-latency endpoints, and cross-request prefix caching for commonly repeated queries
[05:64] Maya: int8 concerns us — how do you validate quality after quant? we need automatic regression checks after any quantized rollout
[05:00] Marcus: Optimize can push a canary with automated evals: create a canary variant, run prompt-set based tests, and gate the rollout on regression thresholds. if a regression is detected, automatic fallback to baseline is supported
[05:13] Nina (not introduced): [laughter] — (note: background)
[05:15] Lena: what about PII — some prompts include user-entered addresses and partial names
[05:20] Alicia: Redwood supports redaction rules in the eval pipeline; you can define patterns to mask PII before artifacts are stored. we also support short retention windows for eval logs per account
[05:30] Jared: ok, pricing — how does pilot pricing differ for hosted vs dedicated?
[05:33] Alicia: pilot pricing options: hosted pay-as-you-go for quicker test (lower commit, slightly higher per-token), or a small dedicated reserved pool if you want guaranteed throughput and data isolation. i'll include line items in the follow-up email
[05:45] Jared: for the pilot we want nightly runs against our top-10k queries, a dashboard, and a regression alert configured for CTR drop >0.5%
[05:53] Marcus: we can do that — recommend three prompt sets: top-queries, personalized queries (with masked PII), and long-form product-description prompts, then we'll wire the nightly job and dashboard
[06:03] [06:03] Priya: feature ask — can we have a programmable threshold expression, like (delta_ctr < -0.5% AND p_value < 0.05) OR (revenue_loss > $X)?
[06:12] Marcus: yes, we have an expression builder in our roadmap; currently you can combine statistical and business thresholds, and i'll log the programmable-expression ask as product feedback
[06:20] Maya: integration tasks — we'll need the API key, sample curl commands, and a terraform snippet to provision the sandbox. can you give temporary credentials?
[06:28] Alicia: yes — we'll provision a sandbox tenant and provide a read-only key for the eval runs. Marcus will attach a terraform snippet and sample curl in the follow-up
[06:35] Tom: SLA question — if we push to dedicated for pilot, what's the latency SLO?
[06:40] Marcus: Dedicated typically hits tail latencies in the 200-300ms range for the model family demo'd today at our configured batch sizes; exact SLOs depend on model and sequence length — we'll run a latency benchmark during the pilot window
[06:50] Naveen: can Optimize recommend sequence-length trimming or token chunking for product descriptions?
[06:54] Marcus: yes — Optimize has a heuristics module that suggests prompt truncation, instruction engineering tips, and chunking strategies to keep costs down without degrading quality, and it publishes tradeoffs in the dashboard
[07:03] [07:05] Marcus: quick demo of how regression alert mail looks — shows affected prompts, delta histogram, and a deep-link to the reproducer run. you can configure the webhook payload to include model metadata and seed
[07:20] Maya: is there a way to batch re-eval older runs after updating metrics or weights?
[07:25] Marcus: absolutely — you can bulk re-run historical runs with a different metric set or mapping function; the system will create a new run id and show diff against the baseline you choose
[07:36] [07:40] Priya: questions from our side — do you support partial rollbacks of experiment segments? e.g., rollback only mobile traffic?
[07:46] Marcus: yes, traffic segmentation supports per-slice rollbacks and canary routing; the serving layer understands experiment ids and routes by header or cookie
[07:54] Lena: for compliance we need to see an immutable trail of prompt inputs for 12 months — can you store eval artifacts that long with customer-managed KMS?
[08:00] Alicia: yes, in Dedicated/Private you can retain artifacts for configurable retention periods and we can enable customer KMS; we will include retention SLA options in the doc
[08:10] Jared: ok, final quick ask — can you seed a small POC with our top-500 queries and produce an A/B report within 5 business days?
[08:18] Alicia: yes, assuming you share the queries today, Marcus and I will scope the POC and confirm timelines — we'll aim for a 5-business-day turnaround
[08:25] Marcus: i'll also attach a sample prompt-set CSV template — includes columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_label, intent_tag, frequency_weight
[08:33] Maya: one more — regression alert noise: will Optimize learn to reduce noise over time?
[08:37] Marcus: the rolling baseline and automatic outlier exclusion help; we also expose sensitivity controls for each metric and experiment, and if needed we'll turn on a two-step gating (informational alert then actionable alert)
[08:46] [08:50] Priya: product ask logged: programmable expressions, per-slice baseline windows, and a CSV importer API for prompt sets
[08:58] Alicia: ok, time check — we have five minutes left, any other blockers?
[09:02] Naveen: security questionnaire — will fill and return by Monday
[09:06] Lena: i'll coordinate with Naveen on the retention table and KMS details
[09:10] Alicia: great. recap — Alicia to send pricing and SOC2 + KMS doc; Marcus to send terraform snippet, sample prompt-set CSV, and dashboard export; Skyline to share top-500 queries and 3 prompt sets; set follow-up POC scoping call next week.
[09:28] Jared: thanks everyone, excited to get started
[09:32] Alicia: thanks all, we'll follow up with the notes and attachments

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — some names and technical acronyms may have minor errors (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache in one auto-caption line). There were light interruptions and background noise on one attendee's line.
